note: Not final doctrine. Not silently promoted into the Declaration. Research required before ratification. Capture clusters index post–Phase 1 ideas with maturity/evidence tags; individual items remain proposed until researched. Includes Local Food / Family Farm Prosperity (CC-PRIN-44), Prosperous Aging System (CC-PRIN-43), Health / Human Capacity / Community Care (CC-PRIN-42), Energy Sovereignty / People’s Energy Dividend (CC-PRIN-41), Civic Wealth / Constitutional Service Investment (CC-PRIN-40), Constitutional Defense / National Resilience (CC-PRIN-39), Citizen-Service Government (CC-PRIN-37/38), Citizen Public Service / anti-aristocracy (CC-PRIN-37), Popular Sovereignty / People’s Branch (CC-PRIN-36), Federalism Doctrine (CC-PRIN-35), Assistance Doctrine (CC-PRIN-34), Family Doctrine (CC-PRIN-32), Human Flourishing Index (CC-PRIN-33), Equal Standing, Constitutional Citizenship, justice, democracy, public-service, transparency, essential systems, human capital, Community OS, Resource Sovereignty, and Food Security spines. Systems Map and Knowledge Graph organize idea sprawl without counting as Phase 2 proof.

items.statement: Power should flow toward people and communities, never permanently away from them.
research_required: empirical effects of decentralization vs competence thresholds

items.statement: Human beings possess inherent dignity and are not merely economic inputs; the people are the principal source of productive capacity, creativity, innovation, and self-government.
conflicts: mere resource language

items.statement: Ownership should become more secure against erosion that converts lasting ownership into conditional tenure.
conflicts: local school/road funding models

items.statement: Ordinary labor should bear the lightest feasible tax burden consistent with constitutional finance.
Education should be treated as productive social investment with shared beneficiaries.
research_required: who benefits from human capital creation

items.statement: Essential transportation and broadband may function as public infrastructure enabling economic participation.
Local communities should possess meaningful food and economic resilience capacity.
Constructive improvement of the common system is among the highest forms of public service.
Local power should be preferred where local institutions are competent (subsidiarity).
conflicts: national functions requiring scale

items.statement: Prosperity should be geographically distributed so staying in a community remains a genuine option.

Justice must protect the public, restrain wrongdoing, repair harm where possible, and return people to productive citizenship whenever safely achievable; it must never become a profit center, a political weapon, or a permanent system of social exclusion.
implications: website domain Justice Safety and Restoration
conflicts: revenue-driven enforcement
punishment-as-default for every social failure

items.statement: Equal justice cannot depend primarily on wealth; money may affect comfort and personal legal choices but must not determine the fundamental quality of justice.
research_required: bail reform evaluations with public-safety controls

items.statement: No justice institution should have a financial incentive to arrest, charge, detain, supervise, fine, or incarcerate more people; the public should fund justice openly.
conflicts: local budgets dependent on fine and forfeiture revenue

items.statement: After lawful completion of a sentence, the system should not quietly continue punishing people forever; residual restrictions must be specific, relevant, reviewable, and limited—not automatic lifetime exclusion.
conflicts: risk-sensitive roles requiring lasting restrictions

items.statement: Political authority is held in trust, never owned; no branch, party, officeholder, donor class, or temporary majority should convert electoral victory into permanent control of the republic.
implications: website domain Democracy Representation and Distributed Government
conflicts: self-protective legislative supremacy
party ownership of offices and districts

items.statement: No temporary majority may use public power principally to make itself harder to remove, harder to investigate, or less accountable to the electorate (anti-entrenchment).
research_required: election administration changes after unified control

items.statement: A political party may support a candidate, but it should not own the office, the district, or the voter; parties should be associations serving voters, not private gatekeepers controlling public offices.
conflicts: strong-party ballot control traditions

items.statement: No political coalition should control legislation, enforcement, adjudication, election administration, ethics enforcement, and district design through the same uninterrupted chain of loyalty.
implications: structural independence under unified party control
conflicts: overbroad multipartisan vetoes that cause paralysis

items.statement: There is a presumption of local authority over genuinely local matters, while constitutional rights remain the floor; state preemption should require a publicly stated statewide necessity.
conflicts: harmful local spillovers
rights-violating local majorities

items.statement: Government work should be among the highest forms of civic service; public institutions should use technology to eliminate unnecessary administrative labor so human talent concentrates in judgment, problem-solving, public engagement, oversight, and service.
implications: Public Service and the 21st-Century State website domain
conflicts: bureaucracy for its own sake
shrink-until-broken minimalism

items.statement: Automate the routine and elevate the human; technology must never become an excuse to remove access for elderly, disabled, rural, poor, offline, or digitally uncomfortable citizens — every digital service needs a real human pathway.
conflicts: digital-only service mandates

items.statement: Preserve professional public-administration expertise while keeping civic leadership and oversight connected to ordinary civic life so career bureaucracy does not become isolated from the public it serves.
conflicts: closed appointment networks
anti-expertise populism that destroys capacity

items.statement: Every board, commission, agency program, and major administrative rule should face periodic review with publicly justified outcomes to renew, reform, consolidate, or end — no public body should exist indefinitely merely because no one remembers why it was created.
conflicts: automatic sunset that destroys useful capacity without review

items.statement: Government services should be organized around the citizen, not agency silos; citizens should not have to understand the organizational chart of government to receive a service, and major agencies should publish honest performance including failures.
conflicts: PR-only dashboards
agency-silo IT that fragments the citizen experience

items.statement: Government should continuously reduce administrative friction while continuously improving public service — eliminating administrative waste without treating service reduction or headcount cuts as ends in themselves.
implications: defining design question beyond more/less government
conflicts: more vs less government as the only frame
cutting services disguised as efficiency
assuming all regulation is waste

items.statement: Government should become invisible in bureaucracy — services work without citizens noticing friction — but never unaccountable: every decision remains explainable, reviewable, measurable, auditable, and constitutionally limited.
conflicts: opacity justified as efficiency
performative complexity

items.statement: Government should operate as a coordinated platform: collect once and reuse securely with appropriate legal authorization so citizens are not forced through duplicated agency paperwork and siloed organizational charts.
conflicts: unlawful data sharing
privacy theater that blocks legitimate reuse
agency IT empires

items.statement: AI may assist government by reducing routine work, but must never become the final decision-maker on matters affecting legal rights or significant benefits; final judgment remains with accountable officials.
conflicts: fully automated adjudication of rights
black-box denials without review

items.statement: Government information created with public resources should be presumed open unless there is a constitutionally or legally justified reason to protect it; the burden should generally be on the government to explain why information is withheld.
conflicts: secrecy as default
everything-is-public absolutism that ignores privacy and safety
unexplained redactions
research_required: state and federal open-records exception inventories

items.statement: In a constitutional republic, government does not own public information; it holds public information in trust for the people, subject only to those limited protections necessary to preserve constitutional rights, legitimate privacy, public safety, and national security.
conflicts: agency ownership of records culture
false tradeoff that transparency must destroy privacy
research_required: privacy/security balancing case law and statutes

items.statement: Every government action funded or authorized by the public should leave a digital trail through a constitutional accountability system — the People's Ledger — so citizens can follow authority, purpose, cost, contracts, audits, and outcomes over time.
conflicts: fragmented unsearchable records
press-release dashboards without failures
invented portal coverage claims before construction

items.statement: Transparency must be equally accessible: routine public records without unnecessary identity barriers; free public-access terminals for those without reliable devices or internet; authentication for sensitive or high-volume access and for any action that changes records; AI may interpret records but never replace the official record.
conflicts: mandatory ID for routine viewing that chills oversight
unauthenticated record alteration
AI answers treated as official law
research_required: records portal cybersecurity and rate-limiting practice
civic AI query evaluation with source citation

items.statement: Essential systems such as banking, insurance, and healthcare should be evaluated through system design — asking how society can reward private innovation and investment while protecting the public interest — rather than beginning from conclusions of inherent corruption.
conflicts: industry-as-villain framing without evidence
reform packages before diagnosis

items.statement: The financial system should primarily reward the creation of productive value rather than the extraction of value.
implications: merger scrutiny and fee transparency research
conflicts: treating all finance as extraction
ignoring legitimate risk allocation and payment functions
research_required: community bank and credit union outcomes

items.statement: Healthy citizens are not simply beneficiaries of society — they are one of its greatest strengths; a constitutional republic should measure success not only by how well it treats illness, but by how well it helps people remain healthy.
implications: mental health, addiction, maternal and child health research
conflicts: illness-treatment-only metrics
unsupported claims that systems are designed to keep people sick
research_required: pharmaceutical incentive studies without predetermined intent claims

items.statement: A preventive society should gradually shift public investment from paying for avoidable crises toward preventing those crises — across healthcare, education, criminal justice, infrastructure, disaster preparedness, environmental protection, and economic development.
conflicts: crisis-only budgeting
assuming prevention always costs less without measurement

items.statement: Major industries and essential systems should be evaluated with a common Essential Systems Test covering long-term value, competition, informed choice, incentive alignment, community strength, transparency, fair risk/reward distribution, investment in people and places, and measurable life improvement.
implications: common screen across banking, insurance, healthcare, pharmaceuticals
conflicts: sector-special pleading without shared criteria

items.statement: Every child should graduate with a meaningful pathway to productive adulthood through multiple respected pathways of equal dignity — including skilled trades, entrepreneurship, higher education, public service, agriculture, manufacturing, healthcare, technology, and the arts — rather than assuming a single model of success.
conflicts: single college-only prestige hierarchy
framing trades as lesser alternatives

items.statement: A constitutional republic should deliberately build human capital infrastructure — institutions whose primary purpose is producing capable, healthy, innovative citizens — with the same seriousness it builds physical infrastructure.
implications: investment in people and productive capacity
conflicts: education as residual after physical capital only
redistribution without capacity-building

items.statement: Regional civic and innovation academies organized around regional economic strengths are one possible institutional model for human capital infrastructure and should be researched and piloted — not locked as a single statewide design before testing — with a mission of making home stronger.
conflicts: statewide one-size curriculum before pilots
success defined as leaving home

items.statement: Human capital pathways should combine real paid work, entrepreneurship of equal seriousness to trades, and civic leadership formation so graduates are ready to build enterprises, serve communities, and lead — not only to be hired.
conflicts: simulated-only work experience
trades without civic or ownership formation

items.statement: The signature of Constitutional Capitalism is playbooks: adaptive community implementation guides that answer how a real town can strengthen and grow over decades — same principles, different local implementation — rather than stopping at what government should do.
conflicts: one-size national template for every town
philosophy without implementation pathways

items.statement: Constitutional Capitalism should operate as a layered architecture — philosophy, constitution, research, implementation, community operating system, national dashboard, and civic improvement network — so proof, playbooks, and continuous citizen improvement remain connected.
implications: four levels from philosophy to case studies
conflicts: book-only or manifesto-only project boundary
dashboards without research integrity

items.statement: Community implementation should begin with assets and people, then attract talent, keep people, and expand ownership — using local prosperity engines and incubator-town patterns adapted to each place's strengths.
conflicts: problem-only inventories
grant-first / building-first without leadership maps
single-employer dependency as the only growth strategy

items.statement: No proposal within Constitutional Capitalism is complete until it includes an implementation pathway, measurable outcomes, estimated costs, anticipated tradeoffs, and a process for evaluation and revision.
conflicts: slogan-only reforms
unmeasured permanent programs

items.statement: Public safety belongs to the community. Police exercise authority on the community’s behalf, courts administer justice in the public trust, and correctional institutions exist to protect society and prepare people for responsible return whenever return is safely possible. The system’s objective is to prevent harm, respond quickly, protect victims, treat addiction and mental illness, hold dangerous people securely, restore everyone who can be restored, and return as many people as safely possible to productive citizenship — not merely to be softer or tougher on crime.
implications: Community Safety, Justice, and Restoration as complete system
system map from prevention through productive citizenship
conflicts: isolated police reform without courts/corrections/reentry
punishment-only or abolition-without-safety framing
profit from human confinement

items.statement: Every community should operate a Community Safety Corps that coordinates sworn peace officers, community officers, behavioral-health response teams, community restoration officers, and victim-service officers — expanding visible human presence while separating community service from coercive authority where a badge and weapon are not required. Success should be measured by relationships, repeat-call reduction, victim satisfaction, trust, clearance of serious crime, and constitutional compliance — never by arrest or citation quotas.
implications: local recruitment pathways and expanded training
conflicts: armed officer as default social worker for every crisis
arrest quotas as productivity
informal favoritism disguised as community roots

items.statement: The state may not create a private financial interest in keeping human beings incarcerated. No private prison, private jail, or private probation company should be paid according to occupied beds, length of confinement, supervision volume, or collected fees. Supporting vendor services may be private, but custody, discipline, sentence administration, release decisions, probation authority, and rehabilitation planning must remain under accountable public control.
implications: durable legal principle over administration-by-administration private-prison policy
conflicts: bed-day or fee-volume private corrections contracting
leaving confinement incentives to changing executive memos alone
research_required: comparative safety and cost analyses with limitations labeled

items.statement: Replace the jail pipeline with a decision system that places people quickly onto proportionate pathways — serious danger, nonviolent accountability, addiction-driven conduct, mental-health crisis, or poverty-related technical violations (inability distinguished from refusal). Prisons should function as secure restoration campuses with individualized plans and reentry beginning on the first day of confinement. After sentence completion, productive citizenship is the destination; Restoration Councils monitor system performance while protecting confidential case information.
conflicts: one-size jail default
jailing for inability to pay
reentry as a last-week checklist
lifetime exclusion without risk-specific justification
research_required: reentry evaluation literature with modest-effect caution

items.statement: Constitutional Capitalism never builds a category of citizens unworthy of reentry. When due process and repeated professional review show continuing extreme danger that cannot be safely managed in the community, the honest category is people whose current, demonstrated danger requires continuing secure custody. No person loses human dignity, even when they lose liberty.
implications: pathway of earned progress even when release is unlikely
conflicts: unworthy of reentry / disposable-person framing
vengeance without current public-safety purpose
exile and banishment as moral substitutes for custody
research_required: victim-safety communication standards for long-term custody

items.statement: For the narrow group requiring continuing secure custody, Constitutional Capitalism uses publicly operated Secure Public Safety Campuses — humane permanent incapacitation with continuing review, graduated custody separated from sentence length, productive contribution without private enrichment, and periodic independent dangerousness review. A risk-assessment score alone is never enough.
implications: Secure Public Safety Campus design agenda
graduated custody levels including medical/geriatric secure care
conflicts: punishment warehouses
score-only permanent custody
maximum security for life by default
coerced nearly unpaid labor enriching private companies
research_required: risk-assessment validation and bias review modules
aging custody cost and misconduct/rearrest evidence

items.statement: Permanent secure custody must be protected against political misuse: only courts may impose it under narrow statutory eligibility; poverty, addiction, disability, homelessness, protest, or unpopular speech can never qualify; exile and private confinement-profit incentives are forbidden; and expensive secure custody should be reserved for those who truly require it through resource concentration.
implications: no private profit from permanent confinement
resource concentration via diversion of non-necessary custody
conflicts: administrative category expansion
overseas or island punishment colonies
bed-day private incentives for delayed release
imprisoning people who do not require secure custody
research_required: First Step Act / compassionate-release comparative state mechanisms
historical misuse case studies of permanent confinement categories

items.statement: Natural resources belong first to the place that bears the extraction, consumption, congestion, pollution, and long-term risk. Private enterprise may profit from using those resources, but the affected community must receive a direct, permanent, and measurable return. The greater the consumption, scarcity, risk, or damage, the greater the obligation to the affected community.
implications: Resource Sovereignty and Community Stewardship as central doctrine
resources are not free inputs merely because a permit can be obtained
links environment, ownership, affordability, and corporate accountability
conflicts: permit-equals-free-resource framing
exporting all surplus while leaving local cleanup and congestion
treating communities as extraction sites rather than inheritors of place-based wealth
research_required: comparative royalty and community-benefit agreement studies

items.statement: Every large resource-consuming project should negotiate a binding Community Resource Compact before public approval, incentives, utility commitments, or infrastructure access. Pricing should be progressive across essential, commercial, intensive, and transformative tiers, charge the total footprint including Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, and pass the Community Carrying-Capacity Test.
conflicts: flat fees that burden households like transformative industrial users
direct-emissions-only accounting that hides purchased-power burdens
approval without disclosure of closure and household-rate effects
research_required: utility rate design and industrial load studies

items.statement: A large share of every resource charge should remain where the impact occurs through protected Local Household Dividend, Community Infrastructure, Resource Restoration, and Future Generations accounts. The majority of geographically concentrated impact revenue must return to the affected place. For exceptionally large projects, communities should also receive continuing ownership interests, not merely one-time fees.
conflicts: spending all extraction revenue during boom years
fees negotiated away with no durable local claim
statewide capture of locally concentrated impact revenue
research_required: sovereign wealth and local permanent-fund models
community equity and royalty design tradeoffs

items.statement: Sector-specific Compacts for mineral extraction, data centers, and warehouses must require full disclosure, bankruptcy-proof cleanup where relevant, and progressive pollution pricing through a durable public Resource and Pollution Ledger. Residential customers should never subsidize the infrastructure or electricity discounts of an extraordinary corporate user.
implications: mining, data-center, and warehouse compact requirements
Resource and Pollution Ledger design agenda
residential rate protection against industrial free-riding
conflicts: extract-then-bankrupt cleanup externalization
data-center incentives that shift costs onto households
relying solely on changeable federal GHG reporting as the permanent ledger
research_required: data-center grid and water impact modules

items.statement: High-resource users should finance locally verified ecological restoration through a Local Carbon Restoration Exchange under an anti-fraud hierarchy that prioritizes avoidance and reduction before offsets. Communities should expand community-owned energy and protect a household essential-energy floor at the lowest sustainable price.
implications: Local Carbon Restoration Exchange design agenda
community solar and local ownership vehicles
conflicts: cheap unverifiable offsets as a license to pollute
replacing one remote corporate energy owner with another without local ownership
industrial rates undercutting household essential use
research_required: community solar and cooperative ownership outcomes

items.statement: Food is critical infrastructure and a strategic community asset. Every community should have the capacity to provide a meaningful share of its essential food needs while remaining connected to broader markets that increase resilience and economic opportunity. Constitutional Capitalism rejects an export-only rule for mass-produced staples because large-scale agriculture and trade help stabilize supply when local harvests fail.
implications: Community Food Security System as broad testable architecture
Local First, Export Second as opportunity not prohibition
conflicts: mass production food becomes export-only
autarky that forbids broader market participation
treating food only as a private retail commodity with no resilience strategy

items.statement: States and regions should develop Regional Food Networks and a State Food Exchange as logistics infrastructure — not government grocery stores — that improve market access for producers, encourage local value-added processing, and connect farms to schools, hospitals, and other institutional buyers while producers remain free to sell into broader markets.
implications: State Food Exchange marketplace design agenda
conflicts: government-operated grocery retail as the primary model
raw-export / finished-import dependency as the only rural pattern
exclusive distant-market reliance with no local offtake opportunity

items.statement: Community Food Security Systems should treat wasted food as wasted human effort, move surplus quickly to people and reserves, maintain emergency food capacity without replacing private markets, and reward farmers for verified soil, water, biodiversity, and carbon stewardship linked to Resource Sovereignty restoration payments.
conflicts: landfill-first surplus disposal
emergency stockpiles that crowd out private markets by design
unverified green claims without measurement

items.statement: Food education and a public Community Food Dashboard are required parts of the system: citizens should understand where food comes from, and communities should improve based on measurable outcomes such as local/regional sourcing, access, affordability, farmer income, waste, reserves, nutrition, and processing capacity — without inventing values before sources exist.
implications: food education in schools and rural academies
conflicts: assumption-driven food policy without measurement
education that treats farming as the only respectable path
research_required: baseline indicator slot design with nulls only

items.statement: Every person stands equal before the Constitution. Neither wealth, office, race, religion, political affiliation, social status, birthplace, celebrity, nor institutional influence shall increase or diminish the protection of the law or the accountability imposed by the law. Equal standing is not identical treatment of every situation: relevant legal differences (such as age or conviction after due process) may matter; status must not determine justice.
implications: complement to Declaration On equality (rejects outcome equality)
conflicts: privilege by wealth, office, or influence
engineered equality of outcome as constitutional mandate
treating every situation identically regardless of relevant legal differences
research_required: selective-enforcement evidence modules without invented rates
constitutional_questions: What distinctions are constitutionally relevant versus status privilege?

items.statement: Blind Stage Principle: Justice should evaluate conduct before identity whenever constitutionally and practically possible — asking what happened, what evidence exists, what law applies, and what harm occurred before asking who the person is, how much money they have, what party they belong to, what neighborhood they are from, or who they know. Guiding phrase: The Constitution should hear the evidence before it sees the person.
implications: ordering of inquiry in justice and enforcement design
civic philosophy distinct from literal courtroom blindness in every case
conflicts: status-first justice
selective enforcement by identity or influence
research_required: procedural designs that reduce irrelevant status cues
limits where identity is legally essential

items.statement: Equality of Opportunity and Equality of Accountability: every citizen receives equal constitutional rights, equal legal protection, equal access to justice, equal opportunity to participate, and equal dignity; every citizen also accepts equal accountability, equal civic obligations, and equal responsibility under the law. No one is above the law. No one is beneath its protection.
conflicts: immunity castes
unprotected castes
research_required: access and accountability measurement agendas with null baselines until sourced

items.statement: Reject privilege in every direction: corporate, political, bureaucratic, and inherited governmental privilege; special treatment by wealth or political influence; selective enforcement, prosecution, and immunity — and also reject arbitrary discrimination against people because they belong to any particular group. The Constitution is the common standard.
implications: Equal Standing Test questions on privileged and disadvantaged classes
conflicts: one-directional privilege critique that ignores other capture forms
research_required: institutional privilege case studies labeled as design research, not invented prevalence rates

items.statement: Equal justice requires equal access: meaningful access to competent legal representation, understandable laws, public records, government services, appeals, and due process — otherwise equality exists only on paper.
implications: links to transparency and public-service spines
conflicts: paper rights without usable pathways
research_required: access-to-justice modules without invented representation or delay statistics

items.statement: Shared civic identity: We may differ in our beliefs, backgrounds, occupations, and experiences, but before the Constitution we are fellow citizens first. Our diversity is real; our equality under the law is non-negotiable.
implications: civic culture against identity-group primacy as the sole political lens
conflicts: reducing citizenship to competing identity blocs
research_required: civic-culture and social-trust modules labeled carefully; no invented polarization cures

items.statement: Self-government requires education. A constitutional republic has a duty to prepare every generation to understand its rights, its responsibilities, its institutions, and its ability to improve society through peaceful civic participation. Citizenship is learned through experience: continuous civic education, practical service, and meaningful opportunities to contribute to community decision-making. The primary question is how to graduate every citizen prepared for responsible self-government — not merely at what age someone may vote.
implications: links to Human Capital investment in people
conflicts: birthday-automatic readiness assumption
rights expansion without capacity building
research_required: civic-education effectiveness modules without invented outcomes

items.statement: Civic education should begin in elementary school through participation, not memorization alone — debate, voting practice, budgeting, school problem-solving, community projects, and presentations to officials — along a developmental pathway from community (ages 5–8) to local government (9–11), state government and evidence literacy (12–14), and applied citizenship (15–18).
conflicts: textbook-only civics
locked national curriculum before pilots

items.statement: Every community should create a real Youth Leadership Council — not symbolic — through which students advise city council and school board, review parks, propose ordinances, recommend budgets, conduct surveys, and organize projects, while adults remain legally responsible.
conflicts: token youth advisory bodies
transferring legal authority to minors
research_required: youth council effectiveness and guardrail designs

items.statement: Constitutional Capitalism does not simply declare that voting begins at 16. It asks under what conditions earlier civic participation could strengthen representative government. One exploratory model: certified civic-education completers eligible for school board, municipal, and local ballot voting, with federal and statewide elections unchanged unless future evidence supports broader reform — to be piloted, measured, and evaluated before broader adoption.
implications: explicit research questions on lifelong voting, informed judgment, trust, school effects, unintended consequences
conflicts: settled national voting-age expansion without evidence
age-only framing without civic preparation
research_required: youth local-voting and civic-curriculum evaluation literature
items.note: Reasonable people disagree; architecture records exploration, not settled policy.

items.statement: Students should graduate civically as well as academically through a Constitutional Citizenship Portfolio demonstrating community service, constitutional knowledge, budgeting, public speaking, teamwork, media literacy, problem solving, a civic project, and leadership experience.
conflicts: purely academic graduation with zero civic practice
research_required: employer/college signaling effects without invented claims

items.statement: Schools should become community laboratories of civic life — hosting forums, citizen academies, budgeting workshops, planning meetings, youth councils, debates, and entrepreneurship programs — while teenagers complete meaningful civic service as contribution (not punishment) and track experiential civic scorecards (meetings attended, ideas presented, volunteering, organizing, budgeting, Constitution literacy, meeting officials, building for community) rather than letter-grade theater.
implications: belonging: I belong to this place
conflicts: schools isolated from community decision-making
service-as-punishment framing
surveillance-style ranking products
research_required: service-learning outcome modules without invented rates

items.statement: Every student should graduate having contributed meaningfully to the civic life of their community. Public education should cultivate informed, engaged citizens through structured opportunities for service, public participation, and democratic practice, while remaining neutral toward political parties, candidates, and viewpoints. Every student should complete meaningful civic service that strengthens democratic participation while preserving complete freedom to choose the causes and viewpoints they support. Government should encourage participation, not ideology.
implications: civic participation goal, not partisan participation
conflicts: graduation credit that requires partisan agreement
school programs favoring one political viewpoint
rewarding ideological conformity
research_required: viewpoint-neutrality compliance patterns for civic credit
complaint and audit designs without invented prevalence claims

items.statement: Rather than traditional volunteer hours alone, students should complete a Civic Service Portfolio throughout middle and high school, earning Civic Service Credits through government participation, community improvement, and civic engagement pathways (meetings, youth councils, parks, food security, forums, lawful nonpartisan election support where permitted, and related activities).
implications: links to food security, Community OS, Youth Councils
conflicts: hours-only volunteerism without civic learning
locked statewide credit schedules before pilots

items.statement: Optional political participation — campaigns, parties, ballot initiatives, advocacy, or issue campaigns — may be recognized for civic credit only under viewpoint-neutral rules: schools may recognize civic participation regardless of viewpoint, but may not require students to support or oppose any candidate, party, or policy position as a condition of graduation. Students may satisfy the same requirement through nonpartisan civic alternatives under equal standards. Public schools must not award campaign credit in a way that favors one viewpoint or pressures students into partisan work.
implications: equal standards for all lawful viewpoints
campaign work never a required graduation pathway
conflicts: required campaign work for graduation
unequal recognition across viewpoints
research_required: legal boundaries for school recognition of campaign activity
items.note: Preserves public trust and constitutional neutrality.

items.statement: Every civic experience should include reflection on problems addressed, government learning, perspectives encountered, evidence that influenced thinking, and process improvements — emphasizing democratic practice rather than predetermined conclusions. Graduates may receive a Civic Achievement Transcript documenting meetings, projects, volunteer hours, leadership, research, presentations, service-learning, and government or nonprofit internships as an educational portfolio of civic merit, not political conformity.
conflicts: reflection prompts that demand preferred political conclusions
transcripts used as ideology scores
research_required: reflection rubric designs that remain viewpoint-neutral
privacy and authenticity safeguards for civic transcripts

items.statement: A nation's greatest long-term asset is not its money, its corporations, or its natural resources. It is the children it raises. Children are the shared responsibility of their families, their communities, and ultimately the constitutional republic until they are prepared to become healthy, capable, independent participants in society — not until they are 'productive.' Worth does not depend on economic output.
conflicts: productive-as-worth framing
abandonment of supporting responsibilities
research_required: childhood well-being modules without invented stats

items.statement: Strong families create strong communities. Strong communities create a strong republic. Public institutions should strengthen families rather than replace them whenever possible — family-first, not state-first.
conflicts: default state substitution for family

items.statement: Care and support should climb a subsidiarity ladder — Child → Family → Extended family → Neighborhood → Community → County → State → Nation — with each level stepping in when the previous one genuinely cannot meet the need.
conflicts: skipping nearer supports by default
research_required: local capacity thresholds without invented coverage stats

items.statement: Intergenerational prosperity means removing unnecessary barriers so generations can remain connected when they choose — attainable homeownership, family businesses, multigenerational housing options, inheritance systems that preserve productive assets, caregiving support, flexible zoning where appropriate, local employment, and connectivity — without forcing families to live together. A Family Wealth System includes homes, farms, small businesses, savings, education, skills, and community relationships, plus knowledge, trust, and local institutions.
conflicts: forced co-residence
barriers that quietly sever voluntary family continuity

items.statement: In a prosperous constitutional republic, no child should lack adequate nutrition because of circumstances beyond the child's control. Implementation begins with parents, extended family, neighbors, schools, faith communities, food banks, local charities, and county resources; the state is guarantor of last resort, not first responder in every circumstance.
conflicts: abandonment if local support fails
state-first default that erases community responsibility
research_required: child nutrition modules without invented hunger rates

items.statement: Investing in maternal health, early childhood development, nutrition, education, mental health, safe housing, literacy, civic education, and apprenticeships is long-term national investment in the republic's future capacity — not merely social spending. Communities should measure child flourishing (nutrition, literacy, health, family stability, civic participation, youth work pathways, adulthood transition) and ask whether children are better prepared than the generation before them — with indicator values null until sourced.
conflicts: output-only childhood success metrics
invented indicator values

items.statement: Every child enters the republic with equal human dignity and equal constitutional worth. The measure of a constitutional society is whether that child has a genuine opportunity to grow into a healthy, educated, capable, and free adult — not because success is guaranteed, but because the community, the state, and the nation refused to neglect the foundations of that opportunity.
implications: Equal Standing and Human Capital alignment
conflicts: neglect of foundational opportunity
guaranteed-outcome promises

items.statement: Constitutional Capitalism is a living constitutional philosophy — supported by research, evidence, policy laboratory, modeling lab, community implementation, civic feedback, public debate, and pilot networks — more durable than a book alone. The book remains an introduction; architecture sprawl must not be mistaken for proof.
conflicts: book-only framing that hides operating systems
architecture counted as completion
research_required: program-layer mapping to official phases without renumbering

items.statement: A Constitutional Capitalism Systems Map should organize major human, community, economy, government, justice, infrastructure, national, and continuous-improvement systems as master architecture — not implementation and not evidence.
conflicts: unordered idea accumulation

items.statement: A Knowledge Graph should connect ideas as nodes and typed relationships (with documented/plausible/disputed/untested classes) so the philosophy becomes AI-searchable without treating graph edges as empirical proof.
conflicts: causal chains presented as settled fact without sources
research_required: ingest capture_clusters and frameworks into nodes

items.statement: Constitutional Capitalism should evaluate itself with a Human Flourishing Index answering whether human life improved and whether proposals measurably increase flourishing across health, family, childhood, education, civic life, ownership, resilience, environment, trust, safety, opportunity, time, volunteerism, culture, and life satisfaction — never GDP alone, and never with invented composites.
conflicts: GDP-only success
architecture-as-measurement
research_required: source first HFI domains with registered evidence

items.statement: No person should be abandoned when unable to meet essential needs. No institution should trap a capable person in dependency. Assistance should protect dignity, strengthen capacity, reward productive advancement, and lead toward the greatest independence reasonably possible. Distinguish security (essential needs shocks will not destroy life) from dependency (rules that punish work, marriage, saving, promotion, entrepreneurship, or property). Objective: protect, stabilize, remove barriers, and build a believable path to income, ownership, and participation — not manage a dependent population.
conflicts: one-size-fits-all assistance
dependency as objective

items.statement: Place every recipient on the correct pathway: (A) permanent protection; (B) childhood and dependent care; (C) caregiving as productive participation; (D) temporary stabilization; (E) working but economically insecure; (F) capable but disconnected with reciprocal engagement after barrier removal. Different circumstances require different responses.
conflicts: uniform work rules for permanent incapacity
treating children as moral welfare recipients

items.statement: Eliminate benefit cliffs. Every additional hour of productive work should leave a household better off. Benefits should phase down gradually so total household resources always rise with earned income; recipients should see earnings, taxes, reduced assistance, and net household income before accepting raises. Exact rates require modeling. Universal benefit-impact calculators should integrate into recipient accounts.
conflicts: cliffs that punish advancement

items.statement: Create one Human Prosperity Account coordinating food, health, childcare, housing, unemployment, disability, workforce, transportation, and energy assistance — showing benefits, eligibility, income, training, phaseouts, appointments, goals, local opportunities, independence progress, and appeal rights — with one accountable local navigator. Coordinate programs; do not build a surveillance system.
conflicts: fragmented agency runaround
surveillance by default

items.statement: Replace case processing with prosperity planning. Technology handles eligibility calculations, reminders, coordination, duplicate detection, income updates, and routine renewals. Human workers become Prosperity Navigators who identify barriers, capacities, local economy needs, durable routes forward, service step-down, and ownership accumulation. Automate the routine. Elevate the human.
conflicts: checkbox case processing as primary human role

items.statement: Guarantee foundations of participation before imposing requirements: childcare, transportation, identification, literacy, healthcare, mental health, addiction treatment, housing stability, internet access, criminal-record barriers, disability accommodation, and local job availability. Do not sanction people for jobs that do not exist, cannot be reached, pay less than childcare, jeopardize necessary medical coverage, or cannot accommodate disability. Pair requirements with supports and independent evaluation.
conflicts: requirements without supports

items.statement: Recognize multiple forms of contribution toward independence: employment, apprenticeship, education, addiction recovery, mental-health treatment, caregiving, community service, disaster recovery, public infrastructure work, entrepreneurship preparation, supervised job search, rehabilitation, and civic service. The standard is active movement toward the greatest independence and contribution available — not paycheck alone.
conflicts: paycheck-only participation tests

items.statement: Build a Community Work Guarantee — not universal basic income — as the organizing alternative for capable adults who cannot find suitable private employment: paid local public/community transitional jobs with wages, expectations, supervision, training, worker protections, and pathways into private employment or public service. Must not replace existing employees or become punitive work camps.
conflicts: UBI as substitute for contribution pathways
punitive work camps

items.statement: Require employers to carry their share. Measure large employers with substantial numbers of full-time workers depending on public benefits. Responses may include wage transparency, predictable scheduling, healthcare or social contributions, childcare partnerships, apprenticeships, profit sharing, worker ownership, and company-wide low-wage employer assessments — never assessments tied to named workers' benefit status that would discourage hiring vulnerable people.
conflicts: permanent public wage subsidy for profitable firms
hiring discrimination via named-worker benefit flags
research_required: employer measurement methods without targeting named recipients

items.statement: Make assistance build assets. Reverse rules that punish saving, reliable vehicles, emergency reserves, business starts, or productive equipment. Encourage emergency savings, retirement assets, education accounts, business capital, home equity, tools, transportation, and cooperative ownership, including matched Prosperity Accounts. Destination is durable independence through income and ownership — not mere roll exit.
conflicts: asset tests that punish prudence

items.statement: Treat addiction, illness, and homelessness as barriers requiring coordinated action — crisis stabilization, treatment, transitional housing, supervised recovery, identification, employment, transportation, and mentors — not abandonment until serious offense. Compulsion only in narrowly defined danger, repeated criminal behavior, or incapacity cases with due process. Support without expectations can become abandonment; punishment without treatment can become a revolving door.
conflicts: abandonment
punishment without treatment
research_required: civil liberties and treatment capacity research

items.statement: Enforce reciprocity fairly. After a realistic pathway is offered, able adults who repeatedly refuse every reasonable opportunity should not receive the same unrestricted support indefinitely. Consequences must be gradual, individualized, appealable, proportionate, never imposed on dependent children, and never eliminate emergency food, shelter, or lifesaving care. Distinguish cannot / temporarily unable / imperfectly participating / refusing.
conflicts: indefinite unrestricted support after refusal
child-punishing sanctions

items.statement: Eliminate fraud without treating everyone as fraudulent. Use verified identity, integrated income reporting, duplicate detection, employer reporting, audit sampling, cross-program consistency, due process, and meaningful penalties for organized fraud. Prioritize organized provider/employer fraud, identity theft, sham contractors, corrupt administrators, and improper billing — not constant humiliation of lawful recipients. Reduce destabilizing administrative burden.
conflicts: universal suspicion cultures
ignoring organized fraud

items.statement: Measure exits correctly. Leaving a benefit roll is not automatic success — people may have found work, lost eligibility through paperwork error, become homeless, moved, gone without food, entered jail, or lost healthcare. Scoreboard: income, employment stability, housing, health, food security, savings, ownership, family stability, repeat enrollment, civic participation, and child well-being. Success question: Did the person become more capable, secure, independent, and connected?
conflicts: caseload reduction as sole success metric

items.statement: Operate county/regional Prosperity and Participation Centers connecting assistance → assessment → barrier removal → treatment/education/caregiving/work → rising income → gradual benefit reduction → savings and ownership → independent participation → mentoring others. Governing councils include recipients, employers, educators, healthcare, disability and recovery advocates, workforce orgs, local government, community organizations, and public employees. Governing promise: feed the hungry, protect children, care for the disabled, honor caregivers, stabilize crisis, refuse to abandon illness/addiction; offer capable people pathways to work, service, learning, recovery, ownership, and citizenship; never punish advancement; never design assistance as a permanent substitute for human potential.
conflicts: fragmented warehousing bureaucracy
indiscriminate cutoff politics

items.statement: The federal government is limited, capable, transparent, and focused — not weak. It exists to protect constitutional liberty, defend the nation, preserve a fair national system, coordinate what communities and states cannot accomplish alone, and restrain powers that exceed local control. Power remains local unless its exercise requires national coordination, national uniformity, or protection of constitutional rights.
conflicts: weak-federalism as abandonment
unlimited centralization

items.statement: The federal government must guarantee constitutional rights across jurisdictions: due process, equal protection, voting rights, speech, religion, association, property rights, equal justice, and protection against arbitrary power. Local authority ends where constitutional rights begin.
conflicts: local majorities overriding rights

items.statement: National defense and foreign affairs — defense, diplomacy, treaties, border security, immigration administration, international trade, national intelligence, and strategic infrastructure protection — remain federal because they cannot be effectively divided among thousands of local governments.
conflicts: fragmented border and treaty regimes

items.statement: The federal government manages currency, federal borrowing, national debt, monetary institutions, national fiscal stability, interstate payment systems, and systemic financial risk, and should be constitutionally required to publish complete, understandable, real-time fiscal records through the People’s Ledger.
conflicts: opaque national debt and spending
research_required: ledger architecture without inventing false real-time claims

items.statement: The federal government ensures interstate commerce remains a fair national marketplace: no destructive internal trade barriers, no manipulation against neighboring states, no incompatible national systems, and no evasion of obligations by moving across state lines — without regulating every ordinary local transaction.
conflicts: internal trade wars
micromanaging local exchange

items.statement: The federal government prevents corporations, financial institutions, technology platforms, political organizations, or other national actors from accumulating power beyond meaningful accountability through antitrust, monopoly control, interstate labor-market protection, securities oversight, national financial regulation, marketplace transparency, and prevention of regulatory capture.
conflicts: state-only regulation of supra-state firms

items.statement: The federal government establishes and helps finance national infrastructure standards and connecting systems while local and state institutions build and operate much of the system. Federal role: coordination, standards, interoperability, and equal national access.
conflicts: federal operation of every local asset

items.statement: The federal government maintains authoritative, publicly accessible national information systems. Government records created with public resources are open by default, subject to limited privacy, safety, law-enforcement, and national-security protections.
conflicts: secret-by-default public records

items.statement: The federal government establishes constitutional floors beneath which states cannot fall, while states and communities remain free to exceed those standards or design different delivery models.
conflicts: race-to-the-bottom floors
one operational model for all

items.statement: Emergency federal coordination for war, pandemics, disasters, financial collapse, major cyberattacks, interstate resource emergencies, and supply-chain failures must be temporary, publicly justified, automatically expiring, subject to legislative and judicial review, and never a permanent expansion of federal control.
conflicts: permanent emergency governance

items.statement: The federal government may redistribute national revenue so every community has reasonable access to essential infrastructure and services, but funding should strengthen local capacity rather than create permanent federal control over local administration.
conflicts: funding as permanent federal administration

items.statement: Before power moves up the competency ladder (individual → family → neighborhood → community → municipality → county/region → state → federal), the higher level must justify why the lower level cannot perform the function, what right or national interest is involved, the narrowest necessary role, how local flexibility is protected, when review occurs, and whether authority can return downward.
conflicts: automatic centralization

items.statement: Every major federal funding program must distinguish national outcome, minimum standard, local discretion, reporting requirement, duration, and exit pathway. The federal government may require outcomes (for example reliable broadband access) without automatically dictating identical institutions, vendors, and administrative structures.
conflicts: grants as soft commandeering

items.statement: Lean federal administration: streamline around functions; every agency faces periodic review — is the function constitutionally federal, duplicated, removable by technology, transferable to states, measurable, and should it be renewed, consolidated, transferred, or ended? Goal: strong enough to protect the republic, restrained enough to respect local self-government, transparent enough that the people can see every power it exercises.
conflicts: agency immortality
fragmented duplication

items.statement: Federal authority assumed for necessity should include pathways for return of authority to states and communities when competence and constitutional rights protection allow.
conflicts: one-way ratchet of centralization

items.statement: State sovereignty and local home rule remain the default for ordinary public life — schools, land use, culture, ordinary policing administration, local food systems, and routine municipal decisions — subject to constitutional rights and national floors. The federal government should not routinely perform these functions.
conflicts: routine federal micromanagement of local life

items.statement: All governmental authority originates in the people and remains held in trust for them. The people are not merely periodic voters; they retain direct constitutional powers to propose, approve, reject, recall, review, and reform government — bounded by fundamental rights.
conflicts: unbounded majoritarianism
unaccountable judicial power

items.statement: Constitute the Sovereign People as a fourth branch and first source of authority: Legislative writes laws; Executive administers; Judicial adjudicates and protects rights; People’s Branch retains ultimate authority to propose, reject, recall, amend, audit, and restructure government without a permanent executive-scale bureaucracy.
conflicts: unbounded majoritarianism
unaccountable judicial power

items.statement: Citizen initiative: verified procedures for local ordinances, state statutes and amendments, and — by constitutional redesign — federal statutes and amendments. Federal initiative requires major legislation and almost certainly amendment.

unaccountable judicial power

items.statement: Referendum: automatic or petition-triggered public votes before specified major laws take effect, including constitutional changes, major public-asset transfers, extraordinary debt, and laws altering elections or initiative rights.
conflicts: unbounded majoritarianism
unaccountable judicial power

items.statement: Citizen veto: signatures may suspend a contested law for a public vote; emergency laws may take temporary effect but expire unless ratified.
conflicts: unbounded majoritarianism
unaccountable judicial power

items.statement: Recall with high safeguards for local, state, and redesigned federal legislative offices. Reject ordinary partisan recall of Supreme Court justices. Require substantial signatures, geography, grounds, funding disclosure, attempt limits, post-election waiting period, and fair replacement.
conflicts: ordinary partisan SCOTUS recall

items.statement: People’s Amendment Process: a third Article V pathway with illustrative dual national votes, multi-state thresholds, legal/fiscal review, deliberation, and supermajority ratification parameters — design only, not locked text.
conflicts: unbounded majoritarianism
unaccountable judicial power

items.statement: Citizen-triggered limited constitutional conventions: subject specified in advance; elected delegates; transparent funding; proposals return to the people; no effect without supermajority ratification.
conflicts: unbounded majoritarianism

items.statement: Citizen audit and investigation: verified petitions may compel public audits, IG review, hearings, conflict investigations, and public reports regarding agencies, contracts, court administration, or public bodies.
conflicts: unbounded majoritarianism
unaccountable judicial power

conflicts: unbounded majoritarianism
unaccountable judicial power

items.statement: Transparent emergency decisions: named votes, written reasoning, disclosed recusals, clear duration, and expedited merits review for nationally important emergency applications.
conflicts: unbounded majoritarianism

items.statement: Public proceedings for high courts: live audio, archived video where practical, accessible briefs, plain-language summaries, disclosures, searchable voting histories, and explanations of procedural dismissals.

items.statement: Three removal paths for federal justices — impeachment; Judicial Accountability Tribunal after council investigation; extraordinary national retention vote only after supermajority triggers — not ordinary partisan recall or poll-driven removal for disliked rulings.

items.statement: Constitutional dialogue: courts, legislatures, executives, states, and citizens share oath-bound constitutional roles; when courts invalidate laws they should state controlling provision, severability, alternatives, and reasoning basis; responses are prospective constitutional or statutory processes.

unaccountable judicial power

items.statement: Anti-wealth safeguards for petitions and ballots: immediate donor and beneficial-owner disclosure, neutral guides, public argument space, fiscal and constitutional analysis, single-subject rules, signature verification, geographic distribution, and anti-deception protections.

unaccountable judicial power

items.statement: Levels of direct democracy: strongest locally; county/regional shaping of shared systems; state initiative/referendum/recall/audit; federal redesign for national initiative, specified referenda, People’s Amendment, citizen investigations, and extraordinary mechanisms.

unaccountable judicial power
